# Does binary DPO improve human behavior ranking without order bias?

2026-11-26 | Anicca Research

**TL;DR.** We ran 32 actual optimization steps across eight LoRA adapters. DPO reached AUROC .5737 on a 64-case test, versus logistic .6362; its raw answer-order gap was .2334 versus weighted SFT .0146. We did not promote it.

![cover](/assets/research/manager-execution-03-binary-dpo-2026-11-26-cover.svg)

Cover: Run03 UCI test, 64 sessions, 8 positive.

## The problem
Our previous weighted SFT improved ranking but still trailed logistic regression. We wanted to test whether DPO changes that result. This is for ML engineers familiar with binary logits and LoRA.

## How we did it
1. We reused cached SmolLM2-135M and the UCI Online Shoppers dataset (CC BY 4.0). Training 32 (5 positive), calibration 64 (10 positive), test 64 (8 positive), with the test slice disjoint from our own Run02.
2. Four methods, seeds 42 and 43, four steps each, rank4, alpha8, batch8, AdamW 3e-4; DPO beta .1. SFT to DPO uses two steps at each stage with a frozen SFT reference. Both option orders are used.
3. We saved eight adapters and individual predictions. The binary DPO loss uses -logsigmoid(beta*(2*y-1)*(d_model-d_ref)). Observed actions are pseudo-preferences, not welfare labels.
4. We calibrated neural predictions on the calibration split and averaged the two answer orders. Logistic was not calibrated. Raw order gap is the mean absolute difference when options are swapped.

![pipeline](/assets/research/manager-execution-03-binary-dpo-2026-11-26-pipeline.svg)

Figure 1. Run03 split and training pipeline, same 64 test cases for every condition.

## Results

| Model | AUROC | Raw order gap |
|---|---:|---:|
| Logistic | 0.6362 | N/A |
| DPO | 0.5737 | 0.2334 |
| Weighted SFT | 0.5592 | 0.0146 |
| Base | 0.5580 | 0.2052 |
| Standard SFT | 0.5558 | 0.0266 |
| SFT to DPO | 0.5547 | 0.0501 |

![chart](/assets/research/manager-execution-03-binary-dpo-2026-11-26-chart.svg)

Figure 2. Actual test AUROC and raw order gap, means across two seeds for trained variants. Source: [Run03 receipt](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca/pull/9516). DPO's ranking improved descriptively relative to the base, while order sensitivity increased.

## Trade-offs and limitations
We chose a small CPU smoke test instead of a full benchmark. Only eight test cases are positive, the four steps do not establish a converged comparison, and SFT to DPO sees different examples in each phase. Logistic and neural probability calibration are asymmetric. Team-wide and pretraining overlap are unknown. No significance, external benchmark, adapter reload parity or product benefit verified. No promotion.

## Reproduce or contribute
Read [the draft PR with code, weights and predictions](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca/pull/9516) and propose a matched-budget multi-seed experiment with an invariance gate.
